'''Nikolai Denkov Denkov''' ({{langx|bg|Николай Денков Денков}}, born 3 September 1962) is a Bulgarian politician who served as [[Prime Minister of Bulgaria]] from 2023 to 2024.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-06-06 |title=България има ново правителство с премиер Николай Денков - По света и у нас - БНТ Новини |url=https://bntnews.bg/news/balgariya-ima-novo-pravitelstvo-s-premier-nikolai-denkov-1236077news.html |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=bntnews.bg |language=bg}}</ref> A member of the [[We Continue the Change|PP]] party, he previously served as Member of the [[National Assembly of Bulgaria|National Assembly]] from 2022 to 2023 and as [[Ministry of Education and Science|Minister of Education and Science]] in 2017 and from 2021 to 2022. Denkov is a physicist, physical chemist and chemist. He is a member of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] and was a lecturer at the [[University of Sofia]].

==Early life==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=February 2024}}
Nikolai was born on 3 September 1962, in [[Stara Zagora]], Bulgaria.{{Citation needed|date=June 2023}} After elementary school, he moved to the Bulgarian capital [[Sofia]], where he graduated from the National Gymnasium for Science and Mathematics in 1980.{{Citation needed|date=June 2023}} In the same year he was a participant at the 12th [[International Chemistry Olympiad]] in Linz (Austria) he won a silver medal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IChO Results retrieved January 11th 2026 |url=http://www.icho-official.org/results/results.php?id=12&year=1980 |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=www.icho-official.org}}</ref>

This was followed by a master's degree in chemistry and pharmacy at the [[Sofia University|St. Kliment-Ohridski University in Sofia]], which he completed in 1987.{{Citation needed|date=June 2023}} In 1993, he defended his [[doctoral thesis|dissertation]] and obtained his doctorate.{{citation needed|date=July 2023}}

For the early part of his career, Denkov worked as visiting researcher in [[JRDC]] (Japan), senior researcher in [[Rhone-Poulenc]] R&D (France), lead scientist in [[Unilever]] R&D (USA), and guest professor in France ([[ESPCI-Paris]] and [[Univ. Lille]]).{{citation needed|date=July 2023}}

==Academic career==
Denkov has been an adjunct lecturer since 1997 and professor of physical chemistry at the University of Sofia since 2008. Between 2008 and 2015 he was head of the faculty for technical chemistry and director of the master's course Disperse Systems in Chemical Technologies. He has been a doctor of chemistry since 2007. He specialized in Japan and at [[Uppsala University]] in Sweden and worked as a senior scientist in the research institutes of private companies such as [[Unilever]] ([[United States|USA]]) and [[Rhône-Poulenc]] ([[France]]).{{Citation needed|date=June 2023}}<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mon.bg/bg/34|title=Министър|access-date=27 December 2021|archive-date=15 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915155107/https://www.mon.bg/bg/34|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://dce.uni-sofia.bg/n_d_denkov_cv.xhtml|title=Department of Chemical Engineering - Prof. Nikolai D. Denkov, Ph.D., D.Sc.|access-date=27 December 2021|archive-date=6 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170206143412/http://dce.uni-sofia.bg/n_d_denkov_cv.xhtml|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2010 he was awarded the highest national award "Pythagoras" for scientific achievements by the [[Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science]]. In 2013 he received the Medal of Honor with Blue Ribbon from the University of Sofia.<ref name="auto1" />

Between 2012 and 2013, Denkov was a member of various working groups in the Ministry of Education and Science and in the Council of Ministers. He actively participated in the development of the concept of the Operational Program ''Science and Education for Smart Growth'' and in the discussions for the Partnership Agreement for 2013–2020 between the Republic of Bulgaria and the [[European Commission]].<ref name="auto1" /><ref name="auto" />

==Civil service career==
From August 2014 to April 2016, Denkov was Deputy Minister of Education and Science in the [[Second Borisov Government|Borisov II government]], responsible for higher education and the European Structural Funds, including the implementation of the Operational Program ''Science and Education for Smart Growth''. From 27 January 2017, to 4 May 2017, he was Interim Minister for Education and Science in [[Gerdzhikov Government|Gerdzhikov's interim government]].<ref name="auto1"/>

In 2019, Denkov was awarded the Solvay Prize of the European Colloid and Interface Society (ECIS) for his research achievements and he was elected a full member of the [[Academia Europaea]].

==Political career==
===Education minister (2021–2022)===
Between 12 May 2021, and 13 December 2021, he was again interim minister for education and science in the acting governments of [[First Yanev Government|Yanev I]] and [[Second Yanev Government|Yanev II]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria|COVID-19 pandemic]]. When after the [[2021 Bulgarian general election|general election in November 2021]] that [[We Continue the Change]] (PP) had the largest congressional faction was and could form a coalition capable of governing, Denkov became the education minister in the [[Petkov Government|Cabinet]] of [[Kiril Petkov]].<ref name="auto1" /><ref name="auto" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bgnes.bg/news/izbirat-kabineta-petkov-novite-ministri-poemat-vlastta/|title = Избират кабинета "Петков", новите министри поемат властта}}</ref>

=== Prime Minister of Bulgaria (2023–2024) ===
[[File:Family photo from 2023 NATO Vilnius summit (53038388599).jpg|thumb|Nikolai Denkov at the [[2023 Vilnius summit|NATO 2023 Vilnius summit]] (Bottom Left next to [[Justin Trudeau]])]]
[[File:Isaac Herzog in Beit HaNassi, November 2023 (GPOHZ0 5476).jpg|thumb|Denkov with Israeli President [[Isaac Herzog]] in Jerusalem, Israel, 6 November 2023]] 
{{Further|Denkov Government}}
Following the outcome of the [[2023 Bulgarian parliamentary election|Bulgarian parliamentary elections]] held in April 2023, on 22 May Denkov was projected to become [[Prime Minister of Bulgaria]] as part of a power-sharing agreement between the two most-voted coalitions, [[GERB—SDS]] and [[PP–DB]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=ГЕРБ и ПП-ДБ правят правителство, Денков и Габриел ще са премиери за по 9 месеца (видео) |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/gerb-i-pp-db-pravyat-pravitelstvo-denkov-i-gabriel-shte-sa-premieri-za-po-9-mesetsa-video-news347932.html |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Dunai |first=Marton |date=2023-05-23 |title=Bulgaria breaks political deadlock with proposed power-sharing deal |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/298fb6e6-40bc-4769-b04b-88dbff3971f4 |access-date=2023-05-24}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Bulgaria agrees government with rotating PMs to tackle corruption |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/bulgaria-finds-government-agreement-with-rotating-pm/ |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref> The deal implied that Denkov would lead the new government for the following nine months, before switching positions with [[Mariya Gabriel]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=6 June 2023 |title=Nikolai Denkov, nuevo primer ministro de Bulgaria |url=https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20230606/nikolai-denkov-nuevo-primer-ministro-bulgaria/2448673.shtml |access-date=7 June 2023 |website=RTVE |language=es}}</ref>

Following extensive talks between the two coalitions involved, as well as the [[Movement for Rights and Freedoms]],<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Bulgaria Finally has a Regular Government (CHRONOLOGY OF EVENTS) |url=https://www.novinite.com/articles/220414/Bulgaria+Finally+has+a+Regular+Government+%28CHRONOLOGY+OF+EVENTS%29 |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=Novinite}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Двучасов разговор между ПП-ДБ, ГЕРБ-СДС и ДПС, сред тях Кирил Петков и Делян Пеевски) |url=https://www.24chasa.bg/bulgaria/article/14596899 |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=24chasa.bg |language=bg}}</ref> an official agreement on the composition of the [[Denkov-Gabriel Government|Denkov-Gabriel cabinet]] was reached on 2 June.<ref name=":4" /> On 6 June, the [[49th National Assembly of Bulgaria]] voted in Denkov's new government, with 132 votes in favor and 69 against.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=6 June 2023 |title=Bulgaria's parliament elects new government led by PM Denkov |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/bulgarias-parliament-elects-new-government-led-by-pm-denkov-2023-06-06/ |url-access=registration |access-date=7 June 2023}}</ref> The new government will focus on fighting Russian influence in Bulgaria's security sector and obtaining membership in the [[Schengen Area]] and the [[eurozone]]. A political crisis prompted Bulgaria to postpone adopting the [[euro]] until 2025. In December 2022, Austrian and Dutch opposition blocked Bulgaria and Romania from becoming members of the Schengen Area.<ref name=rfeden>{{cite news |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/bulgaria-parliament-approves-new-government-denkov/32447233.html |title=Bulgarian Parliament Approves Coalition Government After Five Elections In Two Years |date=6 June 2023 |publisher=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty}}</ref>

In September 2023, Denkov called [[Azerbaijan]] a "valuable partner" of Bulgaria.<ref>{{cite news |title=Prime Minister Denkov: Azerbaijan is our valuable partner |url=https://3e-news.net/en/a/view/46885/prime-minister-denkov-azerbaijan-is-our-valuable-partner |work=3E News |date=13 September 2023}}</ref> Denkov condemned [[Hamas]]' actions during the [[Gaza war]] and expressed his support to [[Israel]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sofiaglobe.com/2023/10/07/bulgaria-condemns-hamas-terrorist-attack-on-israel/|title=Bulgaria condemns Hamas terrorist attack on Israel|date=7 October 2023|publisher=The Sofia Globe|archive-date=October 7, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007214254/https://sofiaglobe.com/2023/10/07/bulgaria-condemns-hamas-terrorist-attack-on-israel/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 30 December 2023, it became clear that Denkov's cabinet had secured membership for Bulgaria in the [[Schengen Area]] by air and sea.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |orig-date=30 December 2023 |title=Press corner |url=https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en |access-date=2023-12-31 |website=European Commission - European Commission |language=en}}</ref> Although further negotiations in 2024 would be required to lift border controls by land,<ref name=":5" /> this was a major diplomatic success for the Denkov-Gabriel cabinet, which aimed for а positive decision regarding Schengen Area membership by the end of 2023 as part of the five government priorities stated in July of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Хаджийски |first=Васил |date=2023-07-26 |title=Управляващите приеха програма с пет основни цели до края на мандата на Мария Габриел |url=https://www.dnevnik.bg/politika/2023/07/26/4511680_upravliavashtite_prieha_pet_osnovni_celi_do_kraia_na/ |access-date=2023-12-31 |website=Dnevnik |language=bg}}</ref>

Denkov resigned on 6 March 2024 as part of the power-sharing agreement with Gabriel.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 March 2024 |title=Bulgaria's prime minister resigns as planned, part of a power-sharing agreement |url=https://apnews.com/article/bulgaria-parliament-government-resignation-rotation-denkov-gerb-f35955cc1db235a0ae955697f3db5342 |access-date=6 March 2024 |website=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> However, on 25 March, Gabriel withdrew her nomination for prime minister after announcing that negotiations on forming a new government with PP-DB had failed, and said that new elections would be held.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 March 2024 |title=Bulgaria's prime minister-designate withdraws after talks between political coalitions fail |url=https://apnews.com/article/bulgaria-government-politics-prime-minister-76b3fd77e11a3b8010e2e29e24cb04e2 |access-date=25 March 2024 |website=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

=== Post premiership (2024–present) ===
On the evening of 1 December 2025 amidst large anger in Sofia over the 2026 Budget proposal that exacerbated the [[2025 Bulgarian budget protests]], Denkov said that 'Provocateurs with masks cannot replace the peaceful protest!'<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2025 
|title=Nikolay Denkov: Provocateurs with masks cannot replace the peaceful protest!
|url=https://fakti.bg/en/bulgaria/1018492-nikolai-denkov-provokatori-s-maski-ne-mogat-da-podmenat-mirnia-protest|website=Fakti.bg}}</ref> Denkov also said that the 2 reasons why they were protesting was because 'the people had been really fed up with the lies and that there were a number of lies related to the Budget that was discussed at the 1st or 2 December 2025.' And the other reason Denkov believes why the Protests have started was because 'The people who are Governing Bulgaria right now were Characterised with a-lot of arrogance and brutal force that they will impose their will which also included the Budget and that the reason for the protests wasn't just the Budget but also because the people were really fed up with it and that they want to say: "stop! It is not working this way!".'<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2025 
|title=Thousands Protest in Bulgaria Against 2026 Budget 
|url=https://www.youtube.com/DXoRh7w5kRm?si=nAVe7dwqLZ7vRSuo|website=Times News}}</ref>
